report.incidentSummary: Starting at approximately 05:10 UTC (10:40 IST) on 2026-10-16, OTP login success dropped from ~97.4% to ~70%, while auth-service error rate increased from ~0.5% to ~4.5%. Internal notification-service metrics showed normal SMS dispatch acceptance (HTTP 202) with flat latency and error rates, while cache memory, hit rates, and latency remained healthy. However, because auth-service log ingestion ceased at 04:54 UTC following an infrastructure log-shipper upgrade (CHG-48221), and handset delivery receipts (DLR) are not instrumented, the underlying cause of the verification failures cannot be conclusively confirmed.
report.rootCauseStatement: The root cause cannot be conclusively established due to lack of observability. The degradation is either driven by external telecom carrier latency causing OTPs to arrive after their expiration window (consistent with PIR-1602), or an internal validation failure/clock skew on auth-service node pool instances following log-shipper agent change CHG-48221. Direct discrimination between these causes is prevented by absent auth-service logs and uninstrumented SMS delivery receipt telemetry.

hypotheses.cause: Downstream SMS provider routing degradation or carrier delivery latency causes OTP SMS messages to arrive at user handsets after their expiration window, leading users to submit expired codes that fail verification.
hypotheses.rationale: Historical incident PIR-1602 demonstrated an identical failure pattern where SMS was accepted by the provider but carrier routing delays caused users to receive expired OTPs. However, notification-service has flat error rates and p95 latency, and DLR receipts are not captured.

hypotheses.cause: Clock skew or NTP drift across a subset of auth-service node pool instances (coinciding with CHG-48221 node pool agent upgrade) causes valid OTPs evaluated on affected nodes to fail expiration checks.
hypotheses.rationale: Node pool log shipper agent upgrade CHG-48221 completed at 04:54 UTC, immediately preceding the cessation of auth-service logs and 16 minutes prior to OTP degradation. However, there is no historical precedent or node clock metric confirming host drift.

hypotheses.cause: Cache memory exhaustion or elevated eviction rates causing premature eviction of OTP verification session keys.
hypotheses.rationale: Cache memory remained steady at ~62%, evictions stayed normal at ~35/min, hit rates were >92% across all keyspaces, and p95 latency remained under 1.3 ms.

facts.statement: auth-service otp_success_rate dropped from ~97.4% to 87.04% at 05:10 UTC and settled between 68.0% and 72.7% through 07:00 UTC.
auth-service error_rate rose from baseline ~0.5% to 2.16% at 05:10 UTC and remained elevated around 4.5% through 07:00 UTC.
auth-service emitted zero logs after 04:54:07 UTC across all severity levels.
Infrastructure change CHG-48221 completed on auth-service at 04:54 UTC, upgrading log shipper agent on the node pool from v2.8 to v3.0.
notification-service metric sms_send_failures remained flat at 2.0 to 3.8 count/min throughout 04:30 to 07:00 UTC.
notification-service latency_p95_ms remained stable between 110.8 ms and 126.2 ms, and error_rate remained ~0.3%.
notification-service logs show 308 OTP SMS messages accepted with status 202 by sms-provider, with no delivery receipt (DLR) logs recorded.
Cache memory remained at ~62%, evictions at baseline ~35/min, and keyspace hit rates between 92% and 95.5%.
Historical incident PIR-1602 exhibited 2-5 minute telecom delivery delays with normal acceptance, while PIR-2004 was an outage with spiked send failures.

inferences.statement: The log shipper upgrade CHG-48221 at 04:54 UTC directly caused auth-service to stop forwarding logs, as auth-service logging ceased immediately at 04:54:07 UTC.
The issue is not caused by cache eviction or memory pressure, as cache performance and hit rates remained stable.

The absence of auth-service application logs and SMS delivery receipt (DLR) metrics prevents distinguishing whether the elevated error rate is due to expired tokens from telecom lag or node-level clock validation failures.

assumptions.statement: Users receiving delayed OTP SMS messages attempt verification with expired tokens, causing auth-service verification rejections and driving up auth-service error_rate.
sms-provider does not provide synchronous delivery confirmation on HTTP 202 acceptance, relying on carrier asynchronous queues.

timeline.event: Change CHG-48221 completed: log shipper agent upgraded from v2.8 to v3.0 on auth-service node pool.
Last log entry recorded from auth-service; all subsequent log ingestion from auth-service stopped.
auth-service otp_success_rate drops sharply to 87.04% and error_rate increases to 2.16%.
OTP success rate drops to ~71.99% and error rate reaches ~4.48%, maintaining this degraded plateau through 12:30 IST (07:00 UTC).
Incident INC-6097 declared as SEV1 by On-call SRE.

confidence.rationale: Confidence is low-to-moderate because direct validation error telemetry and carrier delivery receipts are missing. The SMS delivery latency hypothesis is supported by past incident patterns, while clock skew is supported by change timing, but neither can be conclusively verified.

# Investigation report: OTP logins failing

**Outcome:** inconclusive · **Stop reason:** deadline · **Confidence:** 0.45 · **Written by:** reporting agent

## Summary
Starting at approximately 05:10 UTC (10:40 IST) on 2026-10-16, OTP login success dropped from ~97.4% to ~70%, while auth-service error rate increased from ~0.5% to ~4.5%. Internal notification-service metrics showed normal SMS dispatch acceptance (HTTP 202) with flat latency and error rates, while cache memory, hit rates, and latency remained healthy. However, because auth-service log ingestion ceased at 04:54 UTC following an infrastructure log-shipper upgrade (CHG-48221), and handset delivery receipts (DLR) are not instrumented, the underlying cause of the verification failures cannot be conclusively confirmed.

**Root cause:** The root cause cannot be conclusively established due to lack of observability. The degradation is either driven by external telecom carrier latency causing OTPs to arrive after their expiration window (consistent with PIR-1602), or an internal validation failure/clock skew on auth-service node pool instances following log-shipper agent change CHG-48221. Direct discrimination between these causes is prevented by absent auth-service logs and uninstrumented SMS delivery receipt telemetry.

## Hypotheses
1. **Downstream SMS provider routing degradation or carrier delivery latency causes OTP SMS messages to arrive at user handsets after their expiration window, leading users to submit expired codes that fail verification.** — `sms-provider`, upstream_dependency_degradation, confidence 0.50, unresolved
   - Supporting: [ev_3, ev_5, ev_12, ev_13, ev_28, ev_33] · Contradicting: [ev_1, ev_2, ev_6]
   - Historical incident PIR-1602 demonstrated an identical failure pattern where SMS was accepted by the provider but carrier routing delays caused users to receive expired OTPs. However, notification-service has flat error rates and p95 latency, and DLR receipts are not captured.
2. **Clock skew or NTP drift across a subset of auth-service node pool instances (coinciding with CHG-48221 node pool agent upgrade) causes valid OTPs evaluated on affected nodes to fail expiration checks.** — `auth-service`, clock_or_timestamp_skew, confidence 0.35, unresolved
   - Supporting: [ev_3, ev_5, ev_11, ev_16, ev_17] · Contradicting: [ev_24, ev_29, ev_32, ev_33]
   - Node pool log shipper agent upgrade CHG-48221 completed at 04:54 UTC, immediately preceding the cessation of auth-service logs and 16 minutes prior to OTP degradation. However, there is no historical precedent or node clock metric confirming host drift.
3. **Cache memory exhaustion or elevated eviction rates causing premature eviction of OTP verification session keys.** — `cache`, capacity_saturation, confidence 0.05, ruled_out
   - Supporting: none · Contradicting: [ev_18, ev_19, ev_20, ev_22, ev_23]
   - Cache memory remained steady at ~62%, evictions stayed normal at ~35/min, hit rates were >92% across all keyspaces, and p95 latency remained under 1.3 ms.

## Facts
- auth-service otp_success_rate dropped from ~97.4% to 87.04% at 05:10 UTC and settled between 68.0% and 72.7% through 07:00 UTC. [ev_3]
- auth-service error_rate rose from baseline ~0.5% to 2.16% at 05:10 UTC and remained elevated around 4.5% through 07:00 UTC. [ev_5]
- auth-service emitted zero logs after 04:54:07 UTC across all severity levels. [ev_4, ev_7, ev_10, ev_14, ev_26, ev_30]
- Infrastructure change CHG-48221 completed on auth-service at 04:54 UTC, upgrading log shipper agent on the node pool from v2.8 to v3.0. [ev_11, ev_16]
- notification-service metric sms_send_failures remained flat at 2.0 to 3.8 count/min throughout 04:30 to 07:00 UTC. [ev_1]
- notification-service latency_p95_ms remained stable between 110.8 ms and 126.2 ms, and error_rate remained ~0.3%. [ev_2, ev_6]
- notification-service logs show 308 OTP SMS messages accepted with status 202 by sms-provider, with no delivery receipt (DLR) logs recorded. [ev_13, ev_25, ev_28]
- Cache memory remained at ~62%, evictions at baseline ~35/min, and keyspace hit rates between 92% and 95.5%. [ev_18, ev_19, ev_20, ev_22, ev_23]
- Historical incident PIR-1602 exhibited 2-5 minute telecom delivery delays with normal acceptance, while PIR-2004 was an outage with spiked send failures. [ev_12, ev_33]

## Inferences
- The log shipper upgrade CHG-48221 at 04:54 UTC directly caused auth-service to stop forwarding logs, as auth-service logging ceased immediately at 04:54:07 UTC. [ev_11, ev_14, ev_16]
- The issue is not caused by cache eviction or memory pressure, as cache performance and hit rates remained stable. [ev_18, ev_19, ev_20]
- The absence of auth-service application logs and SMS delivery receipt (DLR) metrics prevents distinguishing whether the elevated error rate is due to expired tokens from telecom lag or node-level clock validation failures. [ev_1, ev_3, ev_5, ev_25, ev_26, ev_28]

## Assumptions
- Users receiving delayed OTP SMS messages attempt verification with expired tokens, causing auth-service verification rejections and driving up auth-service error_rate.
- sms-provider does not provide synchronous delivery confirmation on HTTP 202 acceptance, relying on carrier asynchronous queues.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-16 10:24 IST (04:54 UTC)** Change CHG-48221 completed: log shipper agent upgraded from v2.8 to v3.0 on auth-service node pool. [ev_11, ev_16]
- **2026-10-16 10:24:07 IST (04:54:07 UTC)** Last log entry recorded from auth-service; all subsequent log ingestion from auth-service stopped. [ev_10, ev_14]
- **2026-10-16 10:40 IST (05:10 UTC)** auth-service otp_success_rate drops sharply to 87.04% and error_rate increases to 2.16%. [ev_3, ev_5]
- **2026-10-16 10:45 IST (05:15 UTC)** OTP success rate drops to ~71.99% and error rate reaches ~4.48%, maintaining this degraded plateau through 12:30 IST (07:00 UTC). [ev_3, ev_5]
- **2026-10-16 11:20 IST (05:50 UTC)** Incident INC-6097 declared as SEV1 by On-call SRE. [ev_3, ev_5]

## Confidence
0.45: Confidence is low-to-moderate because direct validation error telemetry and carrier delivery receipts are missing. The SMS delivery latency hypothesis is supported by past incident patterns, while clock skew is supported by change timing, but neither can be conclusively verified.

## Gaps
- auth-service logs completely ceased ingestion after 04:54:07 UTC following CHG-48221. (impact: Prevented reading exact OTP validation rejection reasons (e.g. expired vs invalid vs system clock error) and inspecting host-level errors.)
- notification-service and auth-service do not collect or ingest SMS carrier delivery receipts (DLR) or handset delivery latency. (impact: Prevented verifying whether SMS messages were delayed by telecom operators in transit.)
